participants.note: Concept ACK and ACKed an earlier commit; discussed HaveCoin implementation details.
Objected to continuing execution on storage corruption or deserialization errors, advocating wholesale fatal aborts.
Objected to aborting the entire node on optional index corruption and questioned the convoluted callback architecture.
ACKed and reACKed after testing; suggested keeping HaveCoin only on CCoinsViewCache.

claims.harm: Aborting the entire node on optional index corruption takes down operating nodes for non-essential failures, and the callback chain to the GUI message box before abort is convoluted.
claims.quote: doing that on a corrupt index seems a bit more questionable -- if the txindex or blockfilter or coinstats indexes fail, I could see it being better

claims.harm: Swallowing deserialization exceptions or catching them without aborting leaves the program continuing despite storage corruption or severe logic bugs.
claims.quote: The program continues, even though there is a clear storage corruption or severe logic bug
claims.settled_by_quote: CDBWrapper::Read() now catches deserialization exceptions and calls FatalReadError() which does LogError -> m_read_error_cb() -> std::abort().

support.reason: I think getting rid of this indirection is great. It reduces a lot of complexity when thinking about the stack of views.
Code review, local unit tests OK!

result.notes: Initial record. ajtowns's objection regarding aborting the entire node on optional index corruption remains open; maflcko's objection regarding continuing execution on deserialization failure was resolved by restructuring CDBWrapper::Read() to abort fatally via FatalReadError.
